chapter: Sue and Patsy Howard in show business
title: Patsy at Paramount and Small's Paradise
summary: Patsy worked as an assistant to Leroy Prinz at Paramount, and left for Small's Paradise in New York, 1944 to 1946.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: Yes, I was more or less with Leroy Prinz when he was at Paramount and I was assistant dance instructor to he and his brother.
What were some of the films?

Oh, my goodness, I can't recall. I think 'Sing You Sinners', I believe, was one, with Bing Crosby, I don't know if that was the name of the picture. I don't know if that was the name of the picture, but I can't recall -- I believe it was 'Sing You Sinners', and I worked at Paramount more than I did any other place.
How did you happen to go to the studios?
Well, you see, they put out a call, you see, and we go for an audition, and that's how I became an assistant, because I could dance pretty well.
So, of course, when I left here, I went to Small's Paradise in New York and I was there for about three years, doing the shows, choreographer and producer of the shows.
I left here in '44 and I was there until '46.
